title: demo app: BaseHarbor-managed exposure must be HTTPS by default using managed PKI certificates
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Problem

The demo application currently starts its HTTP server with `ListenAndServe()` and is exposed as plain HTTP.

That violates the BaseHarbor product rule:

> Anything created, started, exposed or mediated by `baha` is secure by default.

A BaseHarbor-managed application exposure must not require the developer to manually create certificates or opt into TLS.

## Required architecture

For a BaseHarbor-managed dev exposure:

```text
BaseHarbor / OpenBao managed PKI
        ↓
issue application/server certificate
        ↓
materialize cert + key into protected runtime state
        ↓
mount/inject into workload through BaseHarbor-owned override
        ↓
demo app serves HTTPS
```

The repository must not contain committed private keys or developer-generated certificates.

The repository-owned `compose.yaml` remains unchanged.

The demo app should consume BaseHarbor-provided TLS bindings, for example conceptually:

```text
BASEHARBOR_TLS_CERT_FILE
BASEHARBOR_TLS_KEY_FILE
```

Exact variable names should follow the canonical BaseHarbor contract rather than inventing a demo-only interface.

## Expected behavior

Normal path:

```text
baha up
```

results in an HTTPS application endpoint automatically.

No additional TLS command should be required from the user.

For dev/local use, a BaseHarbor-managed private/self-signed CA is acceptable; the certificate must still be issued and managed through the platform PKI flow rather than embedded in the demo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] BaseHarbor-managed demo exposure is HTTPS by default.
- [ ] The demo app can start TLS from BaseHarbor-provided certificate/key bindings.
- [ ] Certificate issuance comes from the managed BaseHarbor/OpenBao PKI flow.
- [ ] No private key or static certificate is committed to the demo repository.
- [ ] Repository `compose.yaml` is not modified to adopt BaseHarbor TLS.
- [ ] BaseHarbor-owned workload overrides provide the required TLS bindings.
- [ ] Health and metrics remain reachable over the HTTPS application exposure.
- [ ] Demo UI developer links use HTTPS.
- [ ] Standalone non-BaseHarbor mode may remain independently usable, but the BaseHarbor path must never silently downgrade to HTTP.
- [ ] Acceptance tests fail if a `baha`-managed demo exposure is plain HTTP.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body:
Demo-side implementation is now in PR #25.

The demo consumes the existing canonical BaseHarbor file bindings `TLS_CERT_FILE` and `TLS_KEY_FILE`, serves HTTPS when present, and fails closed when BaseHarbor runtime identity is present but TLS bindings are missing.

Important platform dependency found while implementing: BaseHarbor currently documents managed OpenBao PKI issuance / automatic certificate renewal as deferred. Therefore #24 should remain open until BaseHarbor itself automatically issues and mounts the application certificate for the managed exposure path. The demo intentionally does not generate, embed, or self-manage certificates as a workaround.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body: Demo-consumer support is implemented in #25: canonical `TLS_CERT_FILE` / `TLS_KEY_FILE`, HTTPS serving, and fail-closed behavior for BaseHarbor-managed execution. This issue should remain open until BaseHarbor itself automatically issues/injects the managed OpenBao PKI certificate and end-to-end acceptance proves the HTTPS exposure.
